dialogues.speaker: Midori
dialogues.text: Well, I'm running out of new stories to tell Kouichi...

dialogues.speaker: Midori
dialogues.text: It's a new story told by Uncle Ramsay.

dialogues.speaker: Midori
dialogues.text: He said he's been to many countries and seen many interesting things. In order to record these things, he wrote something called the travelogue.

dialogues.speaker: Midori
dialogues.text: He showed me a lot of his travelogues!

dialogues.speaker: Midori
dialogues.text: For example, there's a kind of iron carriage that flies in the sky in Fontaine. It runs along an invisible road. It takes no time to travel from one end of the village to the other.

dialogues.speaker: Midori
dialogues.text: There's a special kind of grass in Sumeru, which can be planted anywhere. It can be planted in soil, water, or sand. Once it's planted, it will sprout and grow.

dialogues.speaker: Midori
dialogues.text: And... And... There's a kind of... hmmm... boat that can stay at the bottom of the sea for a long time!

dialogues.speaker: Midori
dialogues.text: By riding in that boat, people can go to the deep sea to do all kinds of things and see all kinds of fish!

response.speaker: Midori
response.text: Anyway, that's what Uncle Ramsay told me...

response.speaker: Midori
response.text: Recently, Uncle Ramsay stopped sending me his travelogue for some reason. So I'm running out of stories to tell Kouichi.

response.speaker: Midori
response.text: I know that Uncle Ramsay has been staying at the Komore Teahouse. I wanted to go find him. But the gatekeeper, Sister Kozue, wouldn't let me in because I'm a kid...

response.speaker: Midori
response.text: You look old enough. Can you help me ask Uncle Ramsay, what happened to those travelogues?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Ehm, I am not that old...

response.speaker: Midori
response.text: Anyway! You look like a reliable person. Please help me!

response.speaker: Midori
response.text: Oh? Are you also interested in reading those travelogues? No problem. Just give them to me when you're finished.

response.speaker: Midori
response.text: I... I'll go with you. Although I can't get in, I can wait for you near the teahouse...

response.speaker: Midori
response.text: Ah, I'm so looking forward to reading Uncle Ramsay's new travelogue.

choices.text: Did he tell you about Snezhnaya?

response.speaker: Midori
response.text: Snezhnaya? Well, I don't think so.
